claims.head: Quality over quantity for Montréal
claims.call: Montréal needs no more than its usual 14.5 unblocked shots per expected goal.
claims.body: Washington has struggled to keep shots to the perimeter (28th of 32), and Montréal makes its shots count: one expected goal for every 14.5 unblocked shots, 2nd in the league.

claims.head: Different shooting spots
claims.body: Washington ranks 5th of 32 for point-shot reliance, toward the point-heavy end; Montréal ranks 24th, toward the down low end.
claims.call: Washington takes a bigger share of its shots from the point than Montréal.

notes.text: K. Guhle has not played this season. N. Dobson is in his usual spot beside M. Matheson. That pair is getting 9:10 a game at 5-on-5, up from 5:12 with Guhle.

O. Kapanen has not played this season. J. Slafkovský is in his usual spot beside A. Newhook and I. Demidov. That line is getting 8:55 a game at 5-on-5, up from 7:36 with Kapanen. C. Kreider has moved into Slafkovský’s old spot beside N. Suzuki and C. Caufield.
A. Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 6% last season.

R. Sandin has not played this season. T. Liljegren is in his usual spot beside M. Fehérváry. That pair is getting 7:02 a game at 5-on-5, down from 8:00 with Sandin. M. Roy has moved into Liljegren’s old spot beside J. Chychrun.

WSH.head: A genuine toss-up
WSH.body: Montréal has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Washington can tip it if it gets to the dangerous areas.

MTL.head: Nothing to separate these two
MTL.body: Montréal has had more of the chances over recent games and Washington has home ice. Montréal can tip it if it gets to the dangerous areas.
